world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Lu, Wen. 2018. Aspects of the Grammar of Tunxi Hui: A Transitional Sinitic Language (thesis); also Hirata 1998 Huizhou fangyan yanjiu. Not openly retrievable; Sinitic doculects described for tone rather than stress.

sources.citation: 茹培月 Ru Peiyue. 2026. 黄山市屯溪方言单字调实验研究 [Experimental study on monosyllabic tones of the Tunxi dialect]. 现代语言学 14(5): 366-375. DOI 10.12677/ml.2026.145412.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Six citation tones for Tunxi (阴平 阳平 阴上 阳上 去 入); no 重音/轻声 content; explicitly says 连读变调 is not yet covered.

sources.citation: Zhang, Minghui & Fang Hu. 2018. Pitch or phonation: on the glottalization in tone productions in the Ruokeng Hui Chinese dialect. Interspeech 2018, 1398-1402. DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2018-1638.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Instrumental study of citation tones (F0, phonation) in Ruokeng Hui; no occurrence of stress/accent/prominence anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: 刘玲玲 Liu Lingling. 2026. 徽语黟县方言研究综述 [A review of research on the Yixian dialect of Hui Chinese]. 现代语言学 14(5). DOI 10.12677/ml.2026.145379.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Literature survey; no stress statement; records that Hirata (ed.) 1998 gives a full synchronic phonology of Yixian (Biyang) including 连读变调 and 儿化, and that Meng 1997 covers all of Anhui Huiyu.

sources.citation: Hu, Yiying & Hui Feng. 2024. Key acoustic cues for the realization of metrical prominence in tone languages: a cross-dialect study. Interspeech 2024. DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-666.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked because of the title; covers Chongqing, Kunming and Xiamen only, no Hui data. Not.

sources.citation: Shao, Bowei & Rachid Ridouane. 2023. On the nature of apical vowel in Jixi-Hui Chinese: acoustic and articulatory data. Journal of the International Phonetic Association. DOI 10.1017/S0025100322000196 (CC BY).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental study; the phonology background says the apical segment 'can be the nucleus of a syllable and a tone-bearing unit, and can undergo tone sandhi'; no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Shao, Bowei. 2020. The apical vowel in Jixi-Hui Chinese: phonology and phonetics. PhD thesis, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open-access (HAL) phonology dissertation on Jixi-Hui with a background phonology chapter; could contain a remark on prosody/stress. Blocked by HAL's Anubis challenge by automated download; a browser download would work.

sources.citation: Hu, Fang & Minghui Zhang. 2014. Diphthongized vowels in the Yi County Hui Chinese dialect. Interspeech 2014. DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2014-32.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Acoustic study of vowels in Yixian Hui; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Meng Qinghui 孟庆惠 (ed.). 1997. 安徽省志·方言志, 第五篇 皖南徽语 (chapter introduction, pp. 411-412). Beijing: Fangzhi chubanshe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the 3-page chapter introduction survives in the Internet Archive (history and causes of internal diversity of Wannan Huiyu); no statement on stress or 轻声. The phonology sections of the chapter were never archived and the original server (61.191.16.234:8080) is dead.

sources.citation: Zhèngzhāng Shàngfāng. 2002. Huīyǔ. In Hóu Jīngyī (ed.), Xiàndài Hànyǔ Fāngyán Gàilùn, 88-115. Shanghai: Shanghai jiaoyu chubanshe.

sources.note: Authoritative survey chapter on the Hui group by the scholar who established it; the 概论 chapters have a standard 语音 section that sometimes covers 轻声.

sources.citation: Hirata, Shoji 平田昌司 (ed.). 1998. 徽州方言研究. Tokyo: Kohbun Press. iii+vii+337 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Standard multi-dialect description of Huizhou (Tunxi, Xiuning, Yixian, Jixi, Qimen etc.) with full phonologies incl. 连读变调 and 儿化 per Liu 2026; Chinese dialect descriptions of this type usually carry a 轻声 (neutral tone) section, which is where a stress-related statement would sit.

sources.citation: Meng Qinghui 孟庆惠. 1997. 方言志 (第五篇 皖南徽语, pp. 411ff). In 安徽省志. Beijing: Fangzhi chubanshe; and Meng Qinghui. 2005. 徽州方言. Hefei: Anhui renmin chubanshe.

sources.note: Provincial gazetteer chapter on Wannan Huiyu (only its 3-page introduction was archived online) and the same author's 2005 monograph; both give phonologies of Tunxi, Shexian, Jixi, Xiuning, Yixian, Qimen where a 轻声/重音 remark may appear.

sources.note: Only modern full grammar of a Hui variety, in English, with a phonology chapter (consonants, vowels, 'a very complex system of tone sandhi'); the most likely place for an explicit statement on stress or its absence and on neutral-tone syllables. Licensed CC BY-NC-ND but the PDF is behind an automated-access block; needs a browser download.
